patch.value: A passing pm test --run row echoes the command's full stdout, including raw ANSI colour codes, so every quiet pass grows with the runner's report

Found while recording linked-test evidence for the note-conflict fix (2026-11-13). pm test --run keeps each run_results row's complete captured stdout and stderr even when the command passed, the context matched and the run was trusted. A vitest-based linked test prints its coloured summary, so a passing two-file run returns 694 B of stdout of which 304 B are ANSI escape sequences (JSON response 2,697 B in total); in TOON the same stdout is one escaped string cell. The reply grows with the runner's report (file count, test names) although an agent only needs the verdict on a quiet pass, and the escape sequences are noise in every encoding. The decision-field projection added for the execution context leaves stdout untouched. Proposal: on a passing, trusted, mismatch-free row, keep a bounded tail of stdout with ANSI sequences removed (or a byte count with a restore selector), keep full output on failing, refused and mismatched rows, and let an explicit selector (for example --full-output) restore it. Duplicate check: searched linked test run stdout ANSI escape passing output, and run_results stdout passing run bounded output; the closed bounded test-run summaries task persists summaries on item records but does not shape the command reply.

A passing, trusted, mismatch-free pm test --run row returns no raw ANSI escape sequences and at most a bounded stdout tail in TOON and JSON; Failing, refused, skipped and mismatched rows keep their full captured output; An explicit selector restores the full output on every row, and the omission receipt names it
A passing trusted linked-test row returns its verdict and at most a bounded, escape-free tail of stdout
A passing row returns the command's full stdout with raw ANSI colour codes
